title: Rune Construction deterministic grammar bounded reference corpus
authority_note: These examples exercise the proposed grammar. They are synthetic QA/design fixtures unless a case explicitly cites a source precedent. Example payload IDs illustrate typed references; they do not declare new canonical spells, rune meanings, costs or balance values.

cases.title: Single reusable source atom
cases.acceptance: Parses to one SOURCE node with payload light and canonicalizes without changing meaning.

cases.title: Directed force flow
cases.acceptance: Parses as a left-to-right THEN chain; MOVE consumes the active context without inventing a cost.

cases.title: Shaped emitted payload
cases.acceptance: SHAPE requires geometry and changes topology only; payload identity remains a typed reference.

cases.title: Shaped ward
cases.acceptance: Ward and geometry remain separate reusable units and serialize deterministically.

cases.title: Detection atom
cases.acceptance: SENSE is valid only with a typed payload/property reference and does not imply a spell conversion.

cases.title: Anchored bind
cases.acceptance: Canonical serialization sorts anchor before target and preserves the owning object's identity outside the grammar.

cases.title: Declared transformation
cases.acceptance: CHANGE requires a declared result reference; the grammar does not decide whether the transformation is permitted, affordable or balanced.

cases.title: Linked output
cases.acceptance: LINK routes the previous output to a declared target without asserting macro==rune-construction identity.

cases.title: Triggered ward
cases.acceptance: The left event/detector gates the right expression and no implicit timing beyond the WHEN relation is invented.

cases.title: Conditional push
cases.acceptance: Parentheses make the gated branch explicit; the parser does not guess mixed-connector precedence.

cases.title: Explicit parallel composite
cases.acceptance: The grouped light sequence and ward are sibling composite branches; no temporal order between WITH siblings is implied.

cases.title: Chained synchronized routing
cases.acceptance: A same-connector chain evaluates left-to-right and canonicalizes to the same AST.

cases.title: Inscribed item-bound ward
cases.acceptance: The rune extension may attach to an Item reference, but Item Definition/instance ownership remains with PPIA-03.

cases.title: Missing required payload
cases.acceptance: Validation rejects SOURCE without payload and reports the missing slot without inventing a default.

cases.title: Unknown atom
cases.acceptance: Validation rejects BLAST because it is not in the candidate atom registry; spell/action names do not auto-promote to atoms.

cases.title: Mixed connectors without grouping
cases.acceptance: Validation rejects the expression and requires explicit grouping instead of choosing precedence.

cases.title: Explicitly grouped mixed connectors
cases.acceptance: The explicit group resolves the structure deterministically and round-trips through the linear representation.

cases.title: Permission-filtered hidden reference
cases.acceptance: Syntax may parse, but labels, existence, counts, diagnostics, export and AI context are filtered before reference resolution; no hidden target fact leaks.

cases.title: Countered or disrupted construction
cases.acceptance: Grammar validity does not imply successful resolution. Counterspell/resistance/disruption are evaluated by adopted runtime rules and later balance contracts.

cases.title: Ambiguous authoritative write recovery
cases.acceptance: If a write response is lost, the client checks operation status/current version before retrying with the same operation ID; it must not duplicate the inscription or silently overwrite a newer version.
